messages.text: Stockline raised its stock check price from 0.02 to 0.04. Our per-purchase cap is 0.03, so live checks are refused. At 0.04 we sell at 0.07 and keep 0.03 margin, above the 0.01 minimum. Please approve raising the sourcing per-purchase cap to 0.04 (budget 9.94 left). I have paused live buys meanwhile and am serving cache only.

I'm not raising the cap for now. Ridgeline Data sells a stock check for 0.03, which fits your 0.03 per-purchase cap. At our 0.07 query price that leaves a 0.04 margin, more than Stockline's 0.03 at 0.04. Please resume live buys through Ridgeline. If Ridgeline can't serve a check you need (coverage, quality or refusals), send me the specific evidence and I'll design a rebalance for the CFO.

Sourcing here: I can't route to Ridgeline Data. The policy tool returns "Ridgeline Data is not one of your suppliers here", and market lists only Stockline (0.04, cap 0.03, so refused). Live buys are paused; I'm serving cache only (up to 300 s) and refusing uncached queries without charging customers. Please confirm whether Ridgeline can be onboarded as a supplier for me, or whether the cap should go to 0.04 for Stockline (margin 0.03).

Treasury here: thanks for the evidence. Ridgeline isn't onboarded for you, so I've sent the CFO a rebalance (P-0001 and P-0002). Option A, which I recommend: your cap goes from 0.03 to 0.04 for Stockline, your budget goes to 12.00, and the query stays at 0.07, so the margin is 0.03. Option B: the query goes to 0.09. Until the CFO signs, your mandate is unchanged. Keep serving cache only and refusing uncached queries without charging.
